..
Issued at 232 PM EDT Mon Oct 5 2026

Pattern / Forecast Synopsis: 

Split flow regime over the CONUS, with deep northern stream trough 
and associated mature surface low moving east of James Bay continues 
its eastward trek into Atlantic Canada, while strong Canadian 
surface high centered over the upper Midwest will move into the 
region with time. Still a pinched pressure gradient overhead leading 
to some breezy NW winds, particularly over NE lower and eastern 
upper where the pressure gradient remains strongest. Surface high to 
move overhead by evening in conjunction with subtle 500mb ridging, 
but will be a quick passage. Zonal flow in the wake of the deeper 
trough will lead to quick system passages through the remainder of 
the week. As such, a weak, moisture starved shortwave barges through 
the region later tonight into tomorrow, delivering the next chance 
of light rain showers. Anticipation is for this to continue through 
the week's end, but with increasingly more northerly system passages 
as broader 500mb ridging builds into the region by the weekend.

Details: 

Sure feels like autumn out there as a seasonable Canadian airmass 
passes through the region. As such, with just a touch of synoptic 
moisture, seeing some lake aided shallow convection in the NNW flow 
areas... too warm for snow, but still potential for a quick hitting 
light shower in the aforementioned NNW flow belts. As much drier air 
builds and flow tapers, anticipating this activity to trend 
downward, and associated clouds confine to the Charlevoix / Antrim 
county shores this evening amid a land / lake breeze interaction. 
Tricky temperature setup tonight as the surface high holds directly 
overhead to start the evening and early overnight. Excellent 
radiational cooling response anticipated to start, with temperatures 
dropping like a rock. Considering that we are to top out in the 50s 
to perhaps low 60s (and current surface dewpoints mixing down into 
the low-to-mid 30s in places), anticipation is that several places 
will quickly drop into the 30s by 6z. 

Caveat to all of this is the next approaching shortwave and 
associated return flow building. Increase in clouds and SW flow will 
be most prominent toward the Lake Michigan shores, which may 
experience a wild ride with temps... plummeting early and then 
rising well into the 40s by sunrise. Elsewhere things remain tricky. 
Pending on how long winds can remain decoupled and skies cloud-free, 
certainly possible for some interior low spots across NE lower and 
north central lower to make a run at 30 degrees (locally colder) 
tonight. With us clinging on for dear life to the growing season, 
this will force my hand into issuing a Frost Advisory for all 
counties EAST of US 131 (including Kalkaska, though the western half 
of the county may not exactly meet criteria). Could get cute with a 
Freeze Warning embedded in the Au Sable Valley and into Rosco and 
Ogemaw, but with uncertainty around how low things will drop and 
generally low confidence in prolonged temperatures below 28 degrees, 
will hold off on this idea. These areas will likely not see temps 
jump until around or after 12z.

So after all of that, next item of business will be rain shower 
potential with this next wave later tonight into Tuesday. Moisture 
leaves a bit to be desires, but sufficient forcing may be just 
enough to drum a few showers up through the morning hours from NW to 
SE across the region. The day won't be a washout and any given 
shower probably lasts maybe 5-10 minutes at most. Deepest moisture 
and best forcing holds over Ontario, but will leak into eastern 
upper and far northern lower. Bigger story from this system will be 
the winds, which look to pick up considerably out of the SW amid 
warm advection. Gusty winds pushing 35mph seem a fair bet along the 
Lake Michigan shores and the highest terrain across interior 
northern lower through the later afternoon hours into the evening. 
The system quickly clears by evening with winds tapering overnight. 

Still not much change in thought from the previous forecaster's 
thoughts regarding the rest of the week. Zonal flow to deliver quick 
hitting systems with breezy conditions throughout the remainder of 
the week. Temperatures will trend a touch milder Wednesday, cooling 
some thereafter as lows dip into the 30s and 40s. Warmer air builds 
into the weekend, with respectably high potential for daytime highs 
to reach back into the 70s Sunday.
